'''Sōma Nakamura Shrine''' (相馬中村神社) is a Shinto shrine located in Nakamura, Sōma City, Fukushima Prefecture. It is also known as '''Myōken Nakamura Shrine''' (妙見中村神社) or simply Nakamura Shrine. The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}} (identified with {{ill|Myōken|en|Myōken|qid=Q10960623|lt=Myōken Bosatsu}}). The shrine serves as the starting point for the {{ill|Sōma Nomaoi|ja|相馬野馬追|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Nomaoi|qq=}} festival.<ref name="minyu-net20211115">{{Cite web|url=https://www.minyu-net.com/news/news/FM20211115-667668.php |title=Sōma Nakamura Shrine to Receive New Grand Torii After Earthquake Damage |publisher=Fukushima Minyu Newspaper |accessdate=2021-11-15}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The origins of Sōma Nakamura Shrine trace back to the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} when {{ill|Taira no Masakado|2=en|3=Taira no Masakado|4=ja|5=平将門|6=de|7=Taira no Masakado|8=es|9=Taira no Masakado|10=fr|11=Taira no Masakado|lt=Taira no Masakado|qid=Q1207652|ja|Taira no Masakado|2=en|3=Taira no Masakado|4=ja|5=平将門|6=de|7=Taira no Masakado|8=es|9=Taira no Masakado|10=fr|11=Taira no Masakado|lt=Taira no Masakado|qid=Q1207652|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Masakado|13=User:Immanuelle/Taira no Masakado|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, the founder of the {{ill|Sōma clan|en|Sōma clan|qid=Q2975379|lt=Sōma clan}}, established a Myōken Shrine in {{ill|Shimōsa Province|en|Shimōsa Province|qid=Q1053695|lt=Shimōsa Province}} during the Jōhei era (931–937). As the Sōma clan moved to the Sōma district, a new shrine was established. By the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}} in the late 16th century, {{ill|Sōma Nakamura Castle|ja|中村城 (陸奥国)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakamura Castle (Mutsu Province)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 相馬中村城|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11582470}} became the clan's northern stronghold, governed by lords such as {{ill|Q11582520|ja|相馬盛胤|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Moritane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11582520}} and {{ill|Sōma Takatane|ja|相馬隆胤|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Takamine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11582545}}.

After the {{ill|Battle of Sekigahara|en|Battle of Sekigahara|qid=Q234188|lt=Battle of Sekigahara}} in 1600, the Sōma clan was briefly dispossessed of their holdings but regained control in 1611, establishing the {{ill|Sōma Nakamura Domain|en|Sōma Nakamura Domain|qid=Q844079|lt=Sōma Nakamura Domain}}. The shrine was built by {{ill|Sōma Toshitane|ja|相馬利胤|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Takatane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8514593}}, the first lord of the Nakamura Domain, near the southwest of Nakamura Castle in 1611. The current main shrine building was constructed in {{ill|1643|en|1643|qid=Q6917|lt=1643}} by {{ill|Sōma Yoshitane|ja|相馬義胤 (相馬中村藩主)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Yoshitane|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8514636}}, the second domain lord, and has been designated as a {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}.

During the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}, {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} led to the removal of Myōken Bosatsu, and the shrine was renamed Sōma Nakamura Shrine.

Another shrine, {{ill|Sōma Shrine (Sōma City)|lt=Sōma Shrine|ja|相馬神社 (相馬市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōma Shrine (Sōma City)|qq=}}, was established in 1880 on the ruins of Nakamura Castle's main keep after the {{ill|Boshin War|en|Boshin War|qid=Q309184|lt=Boshin War}}.

The shrine has been under the care of the Tashiro family, who have served as hereditary priests since its establishment.

The shrine formerly maintained stables for horses, including retired racehorses such as {{ill|Bashi Ken|ja|バシケーン|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Basikeen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11327620}} (winner of the 2010 Nakayama Grand Jump) and {{ill|Million Disk|ja|ミリオンディスク|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Million Disc|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17225165}} (winner of the 2009 Capella Stakes). However, the stables were dismantled around 2019.<ref>[https://news.netkeiba.com/?pid=news_view&no=72447 Basikeen Finds a New Home at Sōma Nakamura Shrine]</ref>
